coachMessages.text: When every column has an even height, Yellow's claimeven strategy dominates. Red gets the even rows — which are the wrong rows to win.

slides.infoProse: Every column has exactly 2 discs (Red at bottom, Yellow above). This all-even board means Yellow's claimeven response is available everywhere. Red needs to claim an odd-row anchor to break the lock.

coachMessages.text: Red breaks the claimeven lock: play center column (col 3). This creates an odd-row anchor and sets up for deeper tactics.

slides.infoProse: By playing column 3, Red gives it odd height (3). The next disc in column 3 would go to an even row (row 3) — but now Red has a foothold in the odd-height territory, breaking the claimeven symmetry.
